findings.issue: Repeatedly used `pkill -f <pattern>` where the pattern appeared in its own shell command line, killing its own shell (exit 143) seven times; diagnosed the cause at turn 60 but never adopted a safe pattern
findings.suggestion: Write the server PID to a file on start and `kill $(cat /tmp/app.pid)`, or use a pkill pattern guaranteed absent from the current command line

findings.issue: Four turns spent trying pip/PIL, pip3, and imagemagick that don't exist in the environment before inventing the crop.html approach
findings.suggestion: Check tool availability with `which` first, or go straight to the browser-based crop trick it eventually used

findings.issue: Guessed agent-browser CLI syntax ('viewport' subcommand, '--full-page' flag) and wrote a screenshot to a file literally named '--full-page'
findings.suggestion: Read `agent-browser skills get core` before first use (it did after the failure — do it before)

findings.issue: The spec's 'default port 3000' requirement was only acted on after all tests and visual polish were done
findings.suggestion: Extract environment/script contract details (ports, env vars, start commands) into an explicit checklist during initial spec reading

findings.issue: Throwaway data-probe python scripts crashed on trivial bugs (dict_keys serialization, wrong path), wasting two turns
findings.suggestion: Keep probe scripts simpler (print keys with list()) or reuse a working probe file instead of new heredocs

summary: An unusually disciplined session: deep upfront recon, correct app built in one pass with zero fix cycles, exemplary systematic debugging of the localhost/IPv6 binding failure, and visual verification against the reference screenshots that went well beyond the test suite. The main blemish is a self-inflicted pkill loop that killed its own shell seven times despite an early correct diagnosis, plus minor CLI/tool fumbling.
